video_title: Practice Media Availability with Jared McCain | October 18, 2026 | OKC Thunder

quotes.speaker: Jared McCain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain on his focus on minor details for the season
quotes.excerpt: fixing the little things, very minor details that are going to be huge for us later
quotes.quote: Fixing the little things, very minor details that are going to be huge for us later down the season, whether it is simple things like boxing out, our spacing, how we are going to attack certain coverages that we have seen. People are crashing the boards a lot more, so rebounding has been a big thing for us. Just taking those details, watching the film, and then applying it in practice against the coaches or against the team.
quotes.social_post: Jared McCain is focusing on the minor details this season, specifically boxing out and spacing, to help the Thunder attack coverages more effectively.

quotes.speaker: Jared McCain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain on maximizing his role and spacing for teammates
quotes.excerpt: seeing what players we have on the floor and being able to maximize my abilities
quotes.quote: Trying to maximize whatever my position is on the floor. Seeing what players we have on the floor and being able to maximize my abilities within that group of five. I think I do a really good job of just spacing and finding windows for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander or Jalen Williams or AJ when they are coming off pick and roll and they are getting doubled. Mark Daigneault has a really smart mind, so he is able to pick up on those pretty easy.
quotes.social_post: Jared McCain says his role this season is about maximizing his spacing to find windows for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Williams when they face double teams.

quotes.speaker: Jared McCain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain on the importance of every possession in playoffs
quotes.excerpt: pretty much that every possession matters, every detail matters
quotes.quote: Pretty much that every possession matters, every detail matters. In the offseason training, you are able to experience that. I was able to see it more in certain things I am doing on the court, like if I miss a shot and I am not staying in my shot or I am getting tired during a possession in training during the offseason, I know it is going to pay off during that playoff time because it is gruesome out there. It is physical, it is a lot of mental strength going out there. It was a good experience for me just mentally to know it is going to take more.
quotes.social_post: Jared McCain on the mental grind of the NBA: Every possession matters and the offseason work is all about preparing for the physical and mental demands of playoff basketball.

quotes.speaker: Jared McCain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain on his unwavering confidence and playoff experience
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I always just have an unwavering confidence
quotes.quote: I feel like I always just have an unwavering confidence, no matter if I play one minute and come in for the last minute of the game or whatever it is. Getting a start in the playoffs is amazing and it is a really cool experience, but the confidence never wavers and it was really cool to play and start in a playoff game for sure.
quotes.social_post: Jared McCain says his confidence never wavers regardless of his role, noting that starting in a playoff game was a cool experience for his development.

quotes.speaker: Jared McCain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain on attacking closeouts and playmaking
quotes.quote: Reading the closeout is huge. This summer was a lot of just making sure somebody had one of the sticks and just trying to get it in my face because a lot of the time they are closing out really hard, but I still feel like I can make those shots. And then obviously reading it, if I can drive and kick, I can playmake off of those and then that opens up the game for another possession if they think I am going to pass it and I can shoot it. A lot of that is going to dictate my game throughout the season.
quotes.social_post: Jared McCain is working on his ability to read hard closeouts, aiming to become a more effective playmaker and shooter to keep defenses guessing.

quotes.speaker: Jared McCain
quotes.summary_phrase: Jared McCain on the source of his confidence
quotes.excerpt: I played up with my brother, I played up like my whole life
quotes.quote: I played up with my brother, I played up like my whole life. If I am playing up with them, the only shots I am going to get are if I am taking the shots and being confident or going to 24 Hour Fitness or the YMCA and then being on the side of the court, you got to step on, even if you are the youngest person out there. My parents and my brother have been huge in just telling me this is what you do. You work too hard to not go out there and be confident and I have always taken that to heart. I am going to trust my work and I am not going to let anything of an opinion waver my confidence.
quotes.social_post: Jared McCain credits his brother and parents for his unwavering confidence, saying he learned to trust his work and ignore outside opinions early on.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on team evolution and player development
quotes.excerpt: every year is a combination of continuity and things that are consistent and then things that evolve
quotes.quote: Every year is a combination of continuity and things that are consistent and then things that evolve. One of the things that evolves, especially when you have guys that are prime age players, pre-prime players, is the guys. It is always the exciting part of the year. I do not think you ever want to start the season fully formed. You want to go into the year getting ready to learn about the team and let the team declare itself and we always try to have the discipline to do that.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault says he does not want the Thunder to start the season fully formed, preferring to let the team declare itself as they learn about their identity.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on player development and defensive instincts
quotes.excerpt: he came into the league as just a very instinctive competitive guy
quotes.quote: He came into the league as just a very instinctive competitive guy and that won the day for him. That combined with his talent was able to get him on the court very early. As time goes on, that is how Lu was. As time goes on and they guard the same guys over and over again and they learn the pictures and they have an understanding of how they are getting attacked thematically, then it really starts to layer an additional awareness, understanding, wisdom that they then apply.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault on defensive development: Players start with raw instinct and competitiveness, but they eventually layer in wisdom and awareness as they see the same attacks repeatedly.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on learning from every game
quotes.quote: I always am careful to make sure that I am talking about that we learn from every matchup. We learn from the regular season and we learn from the playoff series that we win. We learned as much from the year before having won the series as we do when we lost to Dallas or when we lost to San Antonio. I just want to contextualize that to make sure that I am not representing that the whole season is just a referendum on the last season.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault emphasizes that the Thunder learn from every game, whether it is a regular season matchup or a playoff series, regardless of the outcome.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on Billy Donovan's coaching transition
quotes.excerpt: he loves to coach, he loves basketball, he loves competing
quotes.quote: He loves to coach, he loves basketball, he loves competing, loves being around it. I do not know how many people, if I am being honest, are humble enough to go in the Hall of Fame in September and then taking an assistant coaching job in May or June, but he is one of them. He is a unique original guy and that is just the latest example of it. He will add tremendous value to them. Mitch, I give Mitch a lot of credit. It takes a lot of humility to add somebody with that pedigree.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault praises Billy Donovan for his humility in taking an assistant coaching role after a Hall of Fame career, calling him a unique original.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on the impact of veteran players
quotes.excerpt: those guys have an outsized impact on the whole
quotes.quote: Those guys have an outsized impact on the whole and they are highly contagious players. It is not limited to them. Chet and Dub have been here now for five years, Shai has been here for four years. We have had some guys that have been here for a long time and they enjoy and appreciate what we have going and what it feels like and they know that part of that, they have a responsibility in. They have helped build that and they have to continue to help build that if they want to continue to live in that house so to speak.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault says the Thunder veterans have an outsized, contagious impact on the team and carry a responsibility to continue building the culture they helped create.

quotes.speaker: Mark Daigneault
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Daigneault on team growth and maximizing potential
quotes.excerpt: it is about every single guy learning how to bring their strengths to the team
quotes.quote: It is about every single guy learning how to bring their strengths to the team. And when the whole is better than the sum of the parts, that is how you know you are maximizing a team. I think we have had a team for a long time now where the whole has been better than the sum of the parts, but that is a year by year challenge and that is a challenge for us this year. That is not guaranteed, we have to make that happen.
quotes.social_post: Mark Daigneault says the goal for the Thunder is to ensure the whole remains better than the sum of its parts, noting that maximizing potential is a year by year challenge.
